text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Irsaeli television interviews Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak. Egyptian Information Minister Safwat el-Sherif syas Mubarak talks about the situation in Jerusalem and the future of the peace process. The television's second channel will broadcast the interview tomorrow.
- The Capital Market Authority all-share index rose to a record level after a long period of declines. The index scored 381.42 points against 370.69 at the previous closure.

- Pope Shenouda of Egyptian copts denies that copts are targeted by Moslem militant groups in Egypt. The Pope says at arrival in Johannesburg that statistics show the number of Moslems killed in terrorism operations is much higher than that of christians.

- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid says the general assembly of the state Holding Company for Mining and Refractories has decided to call Egyptian investors to subscribe in a new cement plant in Beni Suef, 120 km (75 miles) south ofCairo. The plant, which will cost 700 million pounds ($206 million), will have an annual capacity of 1.7 million tonnes.
- Information Minister Safwat el-Sherif says Mubarak will issue a decree establishing Sinai Development Authority and South Valley Development Authority.
- Ukrainian Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko arrives in Cairo today on an official visit at the invitation of Egyptian Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri.
- Mubarak will inaugurate the anuual economic conference of the ruling National Democratic Party tomorrow morning.
